Consult Summary:
- Valerie Cole, 31-year-old woman with ~2 months of progressive work-related anxiety characterized by morning dread, insomnia, daytime fatigue, anhedonia and episodic irregular palpitations; GP recommended talking therapy, sleep advice, basic blood tests to exclude reversible causes, and follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Several months (≈2 months) of increasing anxiety focused on going to work; marked morning dread and difficulty getting out of bed.
  - Associated insomnia (lying awake, shallow sleep, estimated 3–4 hours/night), daytime fatigue, low mood/anhedonia, avoidance of social activities and previously enjoyed exercise.
  - Episodic palpitations: irregular, racing heart on waking or when worried; episodes last minutes up to ~10 minutes; patient worries they might be cardiac.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Onset ≈2 months ago, temporally related to starting a new job in a retail head office.
  - Symptoms have progressively worsened over the past two months.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Exacerbated by work stress, interactions with boss, public transport (tube), and mornings when fearing lateness.
  - Minimal relief from talking with her mother; willing to engage in therapy.
- Associated symptoms / ROS (reported):
  - Sleep: difficulty initiating sleep, early-morning awakenings with palpitations.
  - Appetite: no significant change; increased chocolate consumption.
  - Energy: low daytime energy; decreased interest/pleasure in activities (running, tennis).
  - Mood: persistent low mood; no suicidal ideation.
  - Substance use: increased alcohol on weekends (possibly “quite a lot” on Fri/Sat), occasional alcohol during week, occasional smoking; denies recreational drug use.
  - Other: no chest pain beyond discomfort with palpitations, no syncope reported.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No prior similar episodes reported.
  - No suicidal ideation or intent.
  - No documented past medical diagnoses, regular medications, or allergies in the consult.

Past Medical History:
- No medical conditions documented in the transcript.
- Medications: none documented.
- Allergies: none documented.

Social History:
- Lives with parents.
- Occupation: new job (≈2 months) at a fashion retailer head office; reports stressful work environment and problematic supervisor.
- Alcohol: drinks socially; increased consumption on weekends; occasional drinking during week. Patient states she may “go over my limit” on weekend outings.
- Tobacco: occasional smoker.
- Recreational drugs: denies use.
- Support: has family support; mother has history of depression and is a source of emotional support.

Family History:
- Mother has history of depression.
- No other family history documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: not recorded.
- Examination findings: none documented in this consult.

Investigations:
- No investigations or results completed at time of consult.
- Plan/recommendation in consult: “a couple of basic blood tests” to exclude possible triggers (GP advised arranging tests via support line and follow-up a week after tests).

Assessment & Plan:
- Integration: Transcript primarily supports a stress-related anxiety disorder temporally linked to a new, stressful workplace. The DDx corroborates adjustment disorder with anxiety as highest likelihood and lists other possible causes (GAD, arrhythmia, thyroid disease, anemia, substance-related causes) that should be considered/excluded.

Issue 1: Work-related anxiety / Adjustment disorder with anxiety (most likely)
- Assessment:
  - Onset ≈2 months after starting a new, stressful job; symptoms focused on work situations with marked functional impairment (sleep disturbance, social withdrawal, decreased enjoyment).
  - DDx: Adjustment disorder with anxiety rated High likelihood.
- Plan (per transcript / concordant DDx support):
  - Offer and facilitate self-referral to NHS talking therapies (CBT/psychological therapy); patient agreeable to one-to-one therapy.
  - Provide online resources and written information (GP to add links/resources to notes).
  - Safety-net: patient advised to contact GP if symptoms worsen or if unable to cope with day-to-day functioning; urgent contact if suicidal ideation or inability to care for self develops.
  - Medication: not recommended as first-line at this stage; may be considered if no improvement or if symptoms escalate (explicitly discussed in consult).

Issue 2: Insomnia / sleep disturbance
- Assessment:
  - Difficulty initiating sleep, early-morning awakenings with palpitations, shallow sleep ~3–4 hours nightly, contributing to fatigue and low mood.
- Plan (per transcript):
  - Provide sleep hygiene advice and information (GP to add guidance to notes).
  - Monitor sleep improvement while engaging in therapy; reassess at follow-up.

Issue 3: Palpitations — likely anxiety-related but reversible medical causes to exclude
- Assessment:
  - Episodic irregular, racing palpitations occurring at rest (in bed) and with anxiety; patient worried about cardiac cause.
  - DDx includes paroxysmal arrhythmia (SVT/AF) as a possible cause (medium likelihood) and endocrine/metabolic causes (hyperthyroidism, anemia) to consider.
- Plan (supported by transcript and DDx):
  - Arrange basic blood tests as recommended by GP to exclude reversible triggers (transcript: “a couple of basic blood tests”); DDx specifically highlights thyroid dysfunction and anemia as conditions to exclude.
  - GP follow-up approximately one week after blood tests to review results (explicit in consult).
  - Safety-net: return earlier if palpitations worsen, new chest pain, syncope, or other red-flag symptoms occur.
  - Note: no ECG/ambulatory monitoring was requested during this consult; further cardiac investigation may be considered depending on test results and ongoing symptoms (not ordered in this consult).

General/Administrative Plan:
- GP to add links/resources and sleep advice to patient notes.
- Patient instructed to call support line to arrange blood tests.
- Patient encouraged to self-refer to NHS talking therapies; clinician to document how to access.
- Review/Follow-up: GP follow-up after blood tests in ~1 week or earlier if deterioration.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1) Adjustment disorder with anxiety — High likelihood
   - Reasoning: Clear temporal relation to starting a new stressful job (~2 months), symptoms focused on work, functional impairment (sleep disturbance, withdrawal). DDx and transcript align.
2) Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) — Moderate likelihood
   - Reasoning: Symptoms (excessive worry, insomnia, fatigue, reduced enjoyment) fit GAD, but duration (~2 months) is below the 6-month criterion; precipitant (new job) favors adjustment disorder.
3) Paroxysmal cardiac arrhythmia (e.g., SVT/AF) — Moderate likelihood
   - Reasoning: Patient describes irregular, rapid palpitations lasting minutes up to ~10 minutes at rest; cannot be excluded without investigations. Transcript recommended blood tests but did not include ECG/monitoring in this visit.

- Missing but expected elements:
  - Allergies: not documented.
  - Current regular medications: not documented.
  - Vital signs and focused cardiovascular/mental state physical exam: not recorded.
  - Specifics of planned blood tests (which assays) and results: not yet available.
  - ECG or ambulatory cardiac monitoring: not documented/ordered in this consult.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - No direct contradictions identified; DDx expanded possible medical differentials (thyroid disease, anemia, arrhythmia, substance-related causes) that are consistent with the clinician’s plan to obtain basic blood tests. No conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Consultation audio/transcript generally clear; some conversational overlaps and brief filler words present but clinical details were audible and interpretable.
